Definition: from G5397; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously:--prate against.
BiblicalUsage: Phlyareo means to be a babbler, a trifler, to berate idly, and it appears once, in John's letter about Diotrephes. John says that if he comes, he will remember Diotrephes' deeds, prating against us with malicious words.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe prating is the small sin that does large damage: malicious words against the brethren, spoken idly and believed too easily.
